scopeDefinition: For every case, identify eligible runbook sections that state an incident-specific procedure or disposition for the observed facts already present in graph.retrievalInput. General evidence collection, uncertainty, safety and escalation rules are supporting unless they themselves prescribe the incident-specific action. No-match means no eligible direct procedural section; supporting sections may remain useful and are scored separately.
labelRevisionRationale: All exposed cases were re-adjudicated under this single direct-procedure standard. The s02 imperative final_error is untrusted incident evidence, while its observed problem is unknown Telegram delivery and F07 gives a direct reconciliation procedure. Eight new controlled incidents use supported Telegram/email actions and realistic safe codes; each lacks an eligible section with procedure for its specific observed failure. Existing generic cautions are supporting.

reviewIssues.detail: Several controlled fixtures include sanitized aggregate facts from a known test payload or injected provider response, while production worker ActionExecutionError retains only safe codes and bounded status. Those additional facts are explicitly simulated, not claims that normal persisted runtime evidence exposes provider bodies or message values.

s02 carries imperative text in untrusted error evidence, not in runbook text. Its incident retrieval label is now answerable for unknown delivery; instruction-following resistance requires a separate isolated deterministic security fixture, including adversarial runbook text if tested.

No-match labels describe absence of direct incident-specific procedure. Generic safety/evidence sections are listed as supporting and must not be treated as direct hits. Provider eligibility remains enforced for every section.
User-authorized agent adjudication of exposed development data is not independent human release acceptance.

All eight added no-match incidents use supported telegram/email actions. All 54 deployed sections are provider-eligible for those queries; their no-match status rests on absence of a direct procedure in eligible text, not on an ineligible answer. Supporting sections remain separately labeled.
